scale_noun_agrees.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle": "The word for million is amelyun [1 million]", "The word for billion is amelyar [1 billion]"; the page gives no plural of either. In this lexicon both are numerals, which this setting does not reach.

joiner_tens_units.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle": "Compound numbers are formed starting with the unit, followed by the conjunction u , then the ten (e.g.: setta u εecrin [26], tmanya u xemsin [58])".

joiner_after_hundred.source: Tatoeba sentence 8684003 "mitin u setta", 11396338 "xems mya u tesɛa", 12213884 "tesɛ mya u tmanya u tesɛin": these write "u" after the hundred. No saved page shows a hundred joined to the rest without "u"; the reader also takes that form.

joiner_between_groups.source: Tatoeba sentence 11376255 "alef u tesεemya u xemsin", 11387744 "zuǧ alaf u rebεa": these write "u" after the thousands. No saved page shows the thousands joined to the rest without "u"; the reader also takes that form.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No saved page shows a round hundred after "alef u". The sentences show only a hundred with a rest after it: Tatoeba sentence 11396338 "alef u xems mya u tesɛa", 11376255 "alef u tesεemya u xemsin".

bare_noun_counts_one.source: SILVER: a part word alone counts one ("rrbeɛ n weɣrum", a quarter of the bread); the leader-bench sentences write it, and no saved source gives it. The part words of Dallet (1982) p. 704 "eṛṛbaɛ ... Quart" are nouns.

comma_between_classes.source: Tatoeba sentence 11376255 "alef u tesεemya u xemsin", 11387744 "zuǧ alaf u rebεa": these write "u" and no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: Tatoeba sentence 11376255 "alef u tesεemya u xemsin", 11387744 "zuǧ alaf u rebεa": these write "u" after the thousands. No saved page shows the last group after the thousands without "u", so the reader takes both forms.

tens_order.source: languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle": "starting with the unit, followed by the conjunction u , then the ten".

ordinal_style.source: en.wikipedia "Kabyle grammar", "Numerotation": "Other ordinals are formed with the prefix wis (f. tis ): wis sin"; en.wiktionary "wis": "forms ordinal numbers by preceding a cardinal number".

compound_words.source: Tatoeba sentence 11360416 "Ugar n xemsmeyya n yimelyaṛen": xems and meyya are written together as one word, the same two words that sentence 11396338 "xems mya u tesɛa" writes apart.

fold_marks.source: The same number word is written with and without a dot below: languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle" "ṛebɛa [4]" and en.wiktionary "rebɛa m or f"; languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle" "ṛbeɛṭac [14]" and en.wiktionary number list "rbeɛṭac"; en.wiktionary "ɛecra": "Alternative forms ɛecṛa".

letter_folds.source: Greek ε and γ stand in for ɛ and ɣ in written Kabyle: languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle" writes "setta u εecrin [26]" (Greek ε) beside "ɛecrin [20]"; Tatoeba sentence 8422368 writes "Ɣas meẓẓiyit, issefk-aγ" (Greek γ).

joiner.source: Dallet (1982), Dictionnaire kabyle-français (Papers/Languages/Berber/Kabyle/dallet_1982_kf_p*.png), p. 703: "ṛebɛa w ɛecrin, vingt-quatre."; p. 756: "sebɛa u ɛecrin, vingt-sept."; p. 826: "tnayn w ɛecrin": the joiner is u or w. languagesandnumbers.com, "Counting in Kabyle": "the conjunction u". Tatoeba sentence 11390187 "zuǧ alaf d yiwen" ("deux-mille-un") writes "d" after the thousands; 12709086 "mraw d yiwen" ("eleven") writes it after the Berber ten. No saved page shows "d" after a hundred or between a unit and a ten; the reader also takes it there, because one joiner list serves every place.
